expected_symptom: A DXC diagnostic names a function by its mangled LLVM symbol instead of the HLSL declaration the user wrote.
reviewed_by: Claude Sonnet independent review (batch-012 step-10; blind 3414)
summary: Reproduces verbatim on main and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: 'error: External function used in non-library profile: \01?CallMeMaybe@@YAHM_N@Z'. The emitter (CGHLSLMSFinishCodeGen.cpp:3405) prints PrintEscapedString(f.getName()) with no demangling, even though hlsl::dxilutil::DemangleFunctionName has existed since 47958a941 (2018-02-12), four months before the diagnostic was added in 4ade2fccc (2018-06-20), and is already called from three other sites. Two further mangled messages reproduced (export-param check at CGHLSLMSFinishCodeGen.cpp:3233; linker kUndefFunction at DxilLinker.cpp:401, also 20/20 releases). Partial, not blanket: DXIL-validator errors naming a library entry point come out readable. Control: the same compiler names the same function correctly in a Sema diagnostic ('redefinition of CallMeMaybe'). Demangling would give the bare name only; llvm-beanz's suggestion to move the diagnostic to Sema is what yields a signature. Clang trunk exits 0 and emits no diagnostic at all for this input (control confirms its diagnostics do surface in that pane), so the rewrite has not solved it.
title: Better demangling for improved error messages
